newsitem.title: USA: Skydivers injured in Virginia crash.
newsitem.headline: Skydivers injured in Virginia crash.

text.p: A twin-engine plane crashed shortly after takeoff into a field near the Orange County airstrip Saturday, injuring 10 skydivers and the pilot.
"It's a miracle they all survived," said Orange County Sheriff William Spence.
Some of the skydivers thrown from the plane rescued others trapped inside the burning wreckage.

The aircraft, which is often used by the local skydiving club, became airborne momentarily at the end of the 3,200-foot-long airstrip and then tumbled into the field shortly after 3 p.m. EST, the sheriff said.
The plane's wings and the tail were sheared off by the impact, but the cabin remained intact, he said.

The skydivers and pilot were taken to Culpepper Memorial Hospital and the University of Virginia Medical Centre. Four were treated and released, one was in critical condition, one serious and four in fair.
None of the injuries were life-threatening, Spence said.
Orange is a town of about 4,000 people located 40 miles northeast of Charlottesville.
